analyst_view.overall: Sabah are 31st of 36 with 3 points and Barcelona 5th with 9, so Barcelona need the win to stay in the top 8, while Sabah, in their first Champions League campaign, want to compete in front of a big crowd at the Olympic Stadium in Baku. Lamine Yamal stayed in Barcelona with a slight ankle problem, along with the injured Rodri, Xavi Espart and Christensen; the numbers already count all four, and Sabah's Aden McCarthy (banned after his red card at Viking) is counted too, with the rest of Sabah's squad reported fit. What is new since this morning: at his press conference in Baku Hansi Flick said the lineup may change after nine games in four weeks and that he wants to give other players minutes, and previews expect Fariñas, Eric Garcia, Gerard Martín and Bernal to start, with Cubarsí likely rested. Raphinha, Pedri, Adeyemi and Gordon are still expected to start, so the change is moderate. Scottish referee Nick Walsh, who gives a lot of cards (5.8 a game), is in charge, and the numbers already count that.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.4 goals (1.1 Sabah, 3.3 Barcelona), already taking off Lamine Yamal (-16.7%), who gives about a fifth of Barcelona's goal involvement, plus Espart and Christensen, and counting both sides' good scoring runs. Flick has now said he will rotate after a heavy run of games, and the expected XI has Fariñas, Eric Garcia, Martín and Bernal in place of regulars, which the numbers can't see; Raphinha, Pedri and Gordon still start, so I only lean a little lower, to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 6.6 of them for Barcelona, who should have most of the ball against a deep Sabah block. Without Yamal, Barcelona's width comes from Adeyemi and Gordon on the wings with Cancelo pushing up, which still sends play down the flanks, and rotation in defence and midfield changes little here, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, already adding Nick Walsh's high card rate (+25.9%) and Sabah's busy recent card record (+10.9%), which fits a side chasing the ball for long spells, and taking a little off for Barcelona's quieter run (-5.2%). That is already a high figure for a game with no rivalry, and Sabah lose McCarthy (counted) but no other defender, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.5 shots (8.9 Sabah, 25.6 Barcelona), already lifted for Barcelona's heavy recent shooting (+10.6%) and Sabah's (+4.3%). Yamal is one of Barcelona's main shooters and the numbers only take his absence off goals, and Flick's announced rotation adds to that, while Sabah's confidence and home crowd pull the other way; on balance I lean slightly lower, to about 33.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target, already raised for Barcelona's sharp recent finishing (+8.5%) against a Sabah defence that has let plenty through. Without Yamal and with several regulars expected to be rested after the record-long trip, Barcelona's attack should be a bit less sharp than its recent form, so I lean a little lower, to about 11.8.
